findings.topic: 1. Trigger: topic tracking, QoS, executor, timer
findings.claim: The watchdog is one rclpy node spun by rclpy.spin, so it runs a SingleThreadedExecutor with the default mutually-exclusive callback group. It has 3 data subscriptions plus /tf, all BEST_EFFORT / KEEP_LAST / depth 1, and a single 0.1 s wall timer that runs the FSM. A topic's last-seen time is the wall-clock time (time.time()) at which the Python callback ran, not when the message arrived and not the message stamp. The only filter is header.stamp.sec > 0.
findings.evidence: zed_watchdog/zed_watchdog/zed_watchdog_node.py:76-91 (QoS + subs), :94 (create_timer(0.1)), :109-111 (topic_callback uses time.time()), :289 (rclpy.spin)
findings.implication: Message reception and stall detection share one Python thread and the non-monotonic wall clock. If the watchdog process stalls, or the clock steps (chrony), it can misjudge a stall.

findings.topic: 1. Trigger: what counts as a stall
findings.claim: In STABILIZING (7 s) and RUNNING, the first topic with now - last_seen > msg_timeout (3.0 s) causes an immediate transition to COOLDOWN. One silent topic out of three, for one camera, is enough. There is no grace period, no N-of-M check and no second signal.
findings.evidence: zed_watchdog_node.py:151-171, :219-224; config/zed_watchdog_default.yaml:19-23 (boot 60, stability 7, msg_timeout 3.0, cooldown 10, max_attempts 50); config/zed_watchdog.yaml:20-24 (max_attempts 5). The launch file loads zed_watchdog.yaml, not the default: launch/zed_watchdog.launch.py:10-14
findings.implication: A 3 s gap in any one of front cloud, rear cloud or right gray image restarts all three cameras.

findings.topic: 1. Trigger: what the relaunch kills
findings.claim: On entering COOLDOWN, transition_to() calls cleanup_and_close_window(). That runs force_kill_zed_processes(), which SIGKILLs (psutil.kill) any process whose comm name contains zed_*_main, or whose cmdline contains both 'zed_multi_camera' and 'launch.py'. It then sleeps 1 s, sends SIGTERM to the gnome-terminal --wait client and waits up to 2 s. The component container's cmdline (component_container_isolated ... __node:=zed_multi_container) matches neither pattern, so the container is not killed directly. Only the `ros2 launch` python process is SIGKILLed. The container most likely dies from SIGHUP when its session leader (ros2 launch in the terminal tab) dies, which is the default action with no graceful sl::Camera::close(). All of this runs inside the executor callback and blocks it for up to about 3 s.
findings.evidence: zed_watchdog_node.py:211-217, :226-261 (target_names, cmdline match, proc.kill, sleep 1.0), :263-275 (terminate, wait 2.0). Container exec/name: zed-ros2-examples/tutorials/zed_multi_camera/launch/zed_multi_camera_delay_separate_three_cams.launch.py:87-107. SIGHUP behaviour: UNVERIFIED on the robot.
findings.implication: Every restart is an abrupt kill of all 3 cameras without a clean close. That can leave the GMSL/ZED X daemon or Argus in a bad state, which leads to slow or failed re-open, boot timeouts and more attempts. It may also leave an orphaned container if SIGHUP is not delivered. Check with `ps -ef | grep component_container` right after a restart.

findings.topic: 1. Trigger: state machine, cooldown and attempt_count
findings.claim: States: WAITING_FOR_TF (waits for any /tf message; tf_timeout_mins 999999) → COOLDOWN (shortened to 1 s) → LAUNCHING (gnome-terminal --wait -- ros2 launch ... cam_serials:=..., boot_timeout 60 s; all 3 topics must be seen once) → STABILIZING (7 s, 3 s stall test) → RUNNING. Any failure goes back to COOLDOWN, which waits 10 s and relaunches. attempt_count is incremented on every launch and never reset, even after hours in RUNNING. When it reaches max_attempts (5 in zed_watchdog.yaml, 50 in the default), the watchdog enters FATAL_ERROR and does nothing more. The process stays alive, so launch respawn=True does not help. Closing the terminal window (process.poll()) also triggers a restart.
findings.evidence: zed_watchdog_node.py:125-136, :138-149, :177-184, :187-209 (attempt_count += 1, never reset), :116-121; launch/zed_watchdog.launch.py:27-28
findings.implication: Spread over a long shift, sporadic stalls exhaust max_attempts, and the robot is then left with no cameras and no recovery.

findings.topic: 1. Container respawn does not reload ZED components
findings.claim: The container is declared respawn=True, respawn_delay=10. The ZED nodes are loaded into it once by LoadComposableNodes from zed_camera.launch.py. If the container process exits, launch restarts an empty container and the components are not reloaded.
findings.evidence: zed_multi_camera_delay_separate_three_cams.launch.py:98-107 (respawn=True); zed-ros2-wrapper/zed_wrapper/launch/zed_camera.launch.py:378-383 (LoadComposableNodes into /zed_multi/zed_multi_container). That LoadComposableNodes is not re-run on respawn is known launch_ros behaviour, UNVERIFIED here.
findings.implication: This explains 'without the watchdog the ZED node simply died': the process exits, an empty container comes back and no topics are published. The respawn flag gives a false sense of recovery.

findings.topic: 1. The wrapper has hard exit() paths that take down all 3 cameras
findings.claim: Inside the grab thread, an unhandled grab error logs 'Critical camera error: ... NODE KILLED.' and calls exit(EXIT_FAILURE). Failing to start positional tracking 3 times also exits. The 3 cameras share one process, so one camera's fatal error kills all three. CAMERA_REBOOTING, CAMERA_NOT_INITIALIZED and FAILURE are handled by sleeping 1 s and retrying, which means topics are silent while the SDK self-recovers.
findings.evidence: zed_components/src/zed_camera/src/zed_camera_component_main.cpp:4580-4611 (grab error handling, exit at :4610), :4436-4446 (pos-tracking exit); front config camera_timeout_sec 35 / camera_max_reconnect 7 (common_stereo_zed_front.yaml:23-24)
findings.implication: Two cases need different handling. 'Process dead' (exit/segfault) is only fixed by a restart. 'SDK self-recovering' can legitimately last longer than 3 s, and the SDK is configured to tolerate up to 35 s × 7. The watchdog kills the camera long before the SDK's own recovery could finish.

findings.topic: 2. False trigger: point cloud dropped on TF lookup failure
findings.claim: The patched publishPointCloud() calls tf_buffer_->lookupTransform('base_link', mPointCloudFrameId, current_timestamp, 0.1 s). current_timestamp is the camera image time. On any tf2 exception it logs a throttled WARN 'Could not transform ... to base_link' and returns without publishing. Two watched topics are clouds, so if TF from the IPC (zenoh /tf, /tf_static) is late, missing or not bracketing the image stamp, the watchdog restarts healthy cameras. Whether this happens depends on whether the base_link→zed_*_left_camera_frame chain is entirely static.
findings.evidence: zed_camera_component_video_depth.cpp:2514-2529 (lookup at image stamp, 0.1 s timeout, return on failure), :64-65 (separate tf buffer/listener). Zenoh allow-list bridges /tf and /tf_static from the IPC: assets/zenoh/zenoh_config.json5:17. Static or dynamic chain: UNVERIFIED (lives on the IPC).
findings.implication: With a static chain, a zenoh hiccup after startup is harmless. With any dynamic link in the chain, IPC↔Orin clock offset or zenoh latency > 0.1 s drops clouds and causes a false restart. Check the camera terminal log for 'Could not transform' just before each 'Runtime Failure'. Fix: use lookupTransform(..., tf2::TimePointZero) (latest), or cache the static extrinsic once.

findings.topic: 2. False trigger: watchdog measures callback time on a non-monotonic clock
findings.claim: last_seen is set from time.time() inside the callback, and the check also uses time.time(). A forward step of the wall clock larger than 3 s (chrony makestep; the robot uses chrony, see jetson_monitor) makes every topic look stale at once. Executor starvation has the same effect, because callbacks and the FSM timer share one thread. If rclpy services ready timers before subscriptions, the first FSM tick after a long stall sees stale timestamps even when fresh messages are queued.
findings.evidence: zed_watchdog_node.py:111, :114, :220; chrony use: jetson_monitor/jetson_monitor_node.py:96-108. rclpy timer-first ordering: UNVERIFIED.
findings.implication: These are low-probability but cheap to rule out. Use time.monotonic() and decouple message reception from the decision.

findings.topic: 2. False trigger: BEST_EFFORT large clouds and DDS fragmentation
findings.claim: The watchdog subscribes BEST_EFFORT. The wrapper publishes RELIABLE, depth 10 (QOS_QUEUE_SIZE). For a best-effort reader, each multi-fragment cloud is lost if any fragment is lost. The repo's cyclonedds.xml sets MaxMessageSize 8192B, so a 100 KB–1 MB voxelised cloud is about 12–120 fragments, with SocketReceiveBufferSize min 10MB. No script sets CYCLONEDDS_URI, so it is unclear whether that file is in effect. The zenoh bridge also pulls many images, including front depth_registered (float32 960x600 ≈ 2.3 MB at 15 Hz), adding to loopback/socket load.
findings.evidence: zed_watchdog_node.py:76-80; zed_components/src/tools/include/sl_types.hpp:95; zed_camera_component_main.cpp:69; assets/dds/cyclonedds.xml:9,12; scripts/run_all_auto_default.sh:46-69 (no CYCLONEDDS_URI); assets/zenoh/zenoh_config.json5:7-16
findings.implication: Dropping every one of about 45 consecutive samples (3 s × 15 Hz) needs sustained loss, which happens mainly when the receiver is CPU-starved. This is plausible under load but not the most likely cause. A watchdog should not need to receive full point clouds just to decide liveness.

findings.topic: 2. GPU load slows the camera pipeline; OD runs in the front grab loop
findings.claim: In the grab thread, each frame runs grab() (front: NEURAL depth at HD1200), processPointCloud (CPU retrieveMeasure), odometry/pose and processDetectedObjects→retrieveCustomObjects. processDetectedObjects returns early when the obj_det topic has no subscribers, and the code comments that OD is asynchronous ('objects.is_new'). The point-cloud thread is SCHED_BATCH and uses try_lock, so a slow cloud thread skips frames. GPU saturation should therefore lower frame rates. A gap longer than 3 s needs a blocking event: SDK camera reboot/recovery, a long CUDA sync, engine (re)build or a hang.
findings.evidence: zed_camera_component_main.cpp:4523-4528 (grab), :4721-4750 (processPointCloud, pose, processDetectedObjects); zed_camera_component_objdet.cpp:1009-1027 (no-subscriber early return), :1099 ('Async object detection'); video_depth.cpp:2425-2460 (try_lock), common_stereo_zed_front.yaml:84,190
findings.implication: A 1.34x heavier OD model reduces headroom but should not by itself silence a topic for 3 s. Look for the blocking event in the camera log and the SDK log. Setting debug.sdk_verbose_log_file is useful.

findings.topic: 3. What jetson_monitor's 'GPU' number is
findings.claim: jetson_monitor reads jetson.stats['GPU']. In jetson_stats that is gpu['status']['load'] = (integrated-GPU devfreq 'load' sysfs value)/10, i.e. the share of time the GPU engine had work, in 0.1 % steps (hence 99.7). It is not SM occupancy and is not per process. jtop() is created with the default interval=1.0 s, while the node samples it every 0.1 s, so each jtop value is repeated about 10 times. '2–3 s at 99.7' means 2–3 jtop samples. GPU clock frequency and throttle state are not recorded, so 99.7 % at a lowered DVFS or thermal clock looks the same as 99.7 % at full clock.
findings.evidence: jetson_monitor_node.py:37 (jtop() no interval), :18 (interval 0.1), :140; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rbonghi/jetson_stats/master/jtop/jtop.py (def __init__(self, interval=1.0); stats['GPU']=gpu['status']['load']); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rbonghi/jetson_stats/master/jtop/core/gpu.py (float(load)/10.0)
findings.implication: From this signal alone you cannot tell whether a GPU spike caused a stall or came from the relaunch, nor which process caused it.

findings.topic: 3. Spike before or after the stall: the relaunch itself saturates the GPU
findings.claim: The restart sequence is: stall detected at T0 (last message ≈ T0-3 s), kill plus about 1–3 s of blocking cleanup, a 10 s cooldown, then relaunch at about T0+11–13 s. Launching 3 ZED X cameras loads the NEURAL and NEURAL_LIGHT depth engines, the custom ONNX→TRT OD engine (the first run after an ONNX swap builds an engine and can saturate the GPU for a long time) and positional tracking. That produces a multi-second burst of GPU load near 100 %. jetson_monitor timestamps are only in /system_status (not bridged to the IPC, not logged) and in the throttled INFO log line.
findings.evidence: zed_watchdog_node.py:177-181, :187-206; config cooldown_sec 10; jetson_monitor_node.py:138 (logs full stats at 1 Hz), :170 (timestamp); zenoh_config.json5 has no /system_status
findings.implication: Before treating the GPU as the cause, align timestamps. If the 99.7 % window lies within [T0-3 s, T0], it precedes the stall and is a candidate cause. If it lies at about [T0+11 s, T0+60 s], it is the relaunch. The user's 'at that moment' is ambiguous.

findings.topic: 3. jetson_monitor overhead and bugs
findings.claim: jetson_monitor is not GPU-heavy (it only reads sysfs through the jtop service), but it is wasteful and fragile. (a) The network timer at 0.1 s forks `ping` and `chronyc` every tick, about 20 fork/exec per second. If the IPC is unreachable, each call blocks up to 0.5 s and starves the single-threaded executor. (b) It logs the whole jtop stats dict at INFO every 1 s. (c) cpu_temp and fan_rpm are assigned only inside the jtop branch but always used, so it raises UnboundLocalError when jtop is down or a key is missing (the known 'crashes when jtop is down'). (d) history_len is 60 samples at 10 Hz, about 6 s, but is published as 'avg_60s'/'max_60s'.
findings.evidence: jetson_monitor_node.py:18-19, :48, :77-117 (ping/chronyc with timeout 0.5), :138, :144-150 vs :177/:191, :27
findings.implication: It is not the cause of GPU spikes. Drop to 1 Hz and add GPU frequency, throttle and temperature fields, so it can diagnose rather than just display.

findings.topic: 4. Per-camera restart feasibility
findings.claim: All 3 cameras are components in one component_container_isolated process (one executor thread per component). Per-camera restart is impossible with process signals. It is possible in principle through the container's composition services (/zed_multi/zed_multi_container/_container/unload_node and load_node), but only when the component can shut down cleanly: the destructor joins the grab and point-cloud threads. That will hang if grab() is stuck in the SDK or CUDA, and any exit() or segfault still takes all three down. zed_camera.launch.py already supports a per-camera container_name, so separate containers or processes per camera need only a launch change.
findings.evidence: zed_multi_camera_delay_separate_three_cams.launch.py:87-107, :192-210; zed_camera.launch.py:289-309 (creates own container when container_name empty), :378-383; zed_camera_component_main.cpp:240-277 (thread join on shutdown)
findings.implication: One process per camera gives fault isolation and real per-camera restart. The cost is separate CUDA contexts: more memory and GPU time-slicing between processes rather than streams in one context. Measure the throughput difference on the Orin (UNVERIFIED).

findings.topic: 4. A better liveness signal already exists in the wrapper
findings.claim: Each ZED node publishes ~/status/heartbeat (zed_msgs/Heartbeat, beat_count) from a 1 Hz wall timer on the node's own executor, independent of the grab thread. It only publishes when subscribed. /diagnostics carries the grab rate, total processing time vs period ('System overloaded' after 10 overloads) and OD processing time. ~/status/health (sl::HealthStatus) is published from the grab loop.
findings.evidence: zed_camera_component_main.cpp:2054-2099 (status topics), :3392, :3424-3433 (1 Hz heartbeat timer), :8945-8985 (callback_pubHeartbeat), :7540-7560 (diagnostics), :8856-8894 (health)
findings.implication: Heartbeat alive but data stalled means the process is alive and the grab or SDK is slow or recovering, so wait. Heartbeat gone plus the process gone means dead, so restart now. This is the key 'dead vs slow' discriminator, and it needs no point-cloud subscription.

hypotheses.cause: H1: The front (or rear) camera SDK hits a transient GMSL/frame issue (CORRUPTED_FRAME, CAMERA_REBOOTING, FAILURE) and self-recovers. Recovery re-initialises the depth and OD modules, which shows up as about 2–3 s of GPU ~100 %. Topics stop for more than 3 s and the watchdog kills everything before the SDK finishes.
hypotheses.mechanism: The grab thread sleeps 1 s per retry on CAMERA_REBOOTING/FAILURE (main.cpp:4580-4596). The SDK allows camera_timeout_sec 35 × camera_max_reconnect 7. msg_timeout 3 s is far shorter.
hypotheses.how_to_confirm: In the camera gnome-terminal and ~/ros2_logs, look for 'Connection issue detected', 'Camera issue detected', 'Grab status degraded' or 'NODE KILLED' within the 5 s before the watchdog's 'Runtime Failure'. Set debug.sdk_verbose_log_file to a path. Check `dmesg -T` / `journalctl -k` for max96712/nvcsi/vi or nvgpu errors at the same time. Check whether only one camera's topic stalled (the watchdog logs which one).
hypotheses.fix: Do not kill on a short data stall while the heartbeat is alive. Wait up to about 30–45 s, in line with the SDK reconnect policy. Fix any hardware or link errors found in dmesg.

hypotheses.cause: H2: GPU oversubscription. Front NEURAL depth at HD1200 + FP32 DEIM (1.34x YOLO26n) + positional tracking + OD tracking + rear NEURAL_LIGHT, possibly at a reduced GPU clock (DVFS or thermal without jetson_clocks), leaves no headroom. A transient pushes per-frame processing far above 66 ms and data rates collapse.
hypotheses.mechanism: GPU load is time-busy %. A low clock or extra work makes the grab loop process slower than 15 Hz. With the OD model change the margin shrank, so stalls became more frequent.
hypotheses.how_to_confirm: Run `tegrastats --interval 100 --logfile ~/tegra.log` (read-only, ships with L4T) during operation. Look at GR3D_FREQ %@MHz, temperatures and power before each restart. Echo /diagnostics for zed_front to read 'Tot. Processing Time' and 'System overloaded'. Compare one run with OD disabled or with the old YOLO26n ONNX. Check whether jetson_clocks runs at boot (scripts/setup_hardware.sh:13-15 is not called from run_all_auto*.sh).
hypotheses.fix: Run `jetson_clocks` at boot. This is a runtime clock setting, not a JetPack or SDK change, so confirm with the user. Reduce the front load with depth_mode NEURAL_LIGHT for the front, or a lower grab resolution (HD1080/SVGA) if 2.95 m OD range allows. Keep the FP32 model and consider DEIM-N over S. Optionally cap the pipeline (grab_compute_capping_fps is hard-coded to 0 at main.cpp:2454).

hypotheses.cause: H3: The cameras are fine, but clouds are dropped because the TF lookup at the image timestamp fails. TF comes late or with a skewed clock over zenoh from the IPC.
hypotheses.mechanism: video_depth.cpp:2518-2528 returns without publishing on any tf2 exception. Both cloud topics are watched, so a TF gap causes a full restart. GPU load is coincidental.
hypotheses.how_to_confirm: Look for 'Could not transform zed_*_left_camera_frame to base_link' in the camera log before restarts. Check during a stall whether the same camera's image topics keep flowing. On the IPC, check whether base_link→zed_* is published on /tf_static (static) or /tf. Check the chrony offset (jetson_monitor time_offset_ms).
hypotheses.fix: In publishPointCloud use tf2::TimePointZero (latest available), or cache the static extrinsic once at startup. Watch heartbeat or images rather than TF-dependent clouds for liveness.

hypotheses.cause: H4: The container process dies (exit(EXIT_FAILURE) in the wrapper, segfault, CUDA/TRT error or OOM). That kills all 3 cameras, and respawn=True brings back an empty container.
hypotheses.mechanism: main.cpp:4610 / :4445 exit paths; one process for 3 cameras; LoadComposableNodes is not re-run on respawn.
hypotheses.how_to_confirm: In the zed launch terminal look for '[ERROR] [component_container_isolated-1]: process has died [pid ..., exit code ...]'. Check `journalctl -k | grep -i -e oom -e nvgpu`. Check whether the respawned container is empty (`ros2 component list`).
hypotheses.fix: Use one container or process per camera and drop respawn=True on the container (the watchdog owns restarts). Record the exit code and last log lines in the watchdog before restarting.

hypotheses.cause: H5: Watchdog-side false positive: executor starvation (it also does blocking kills), a wall-clock step, or best-effort fragment loss of large clouds.
hypotheses.mechanism: time.time() and the single-threaded executor (zed_watchdog_node.py:111, :220, :289); BEST_EFFORT reader of multi-fragment clouds (cyclonedds.xml MaxMessageSize 8192B).
hypotheses.how_to_confirm: Run `ros2 topic hz /zed_multi/zed_front/point_cloud/cloud_registered` (reliable by default) alongside the watchdog and compare gaps. Log `chronyc tracking` steps. Log the time between consecutive fsm_loop ticks inside the watchdog.
hypotheses.fix: Use time.monotonic(). Use heartbeat plus lightweight topics (camera_info, or the cloud only via a header-only check). Run subscriptions and the FSM in separate callback groups with a MultiThreadedExecutor, and make kills non-blocking.

recommendations: Diagnose before changing anything. For the next few incidents, align three timestamps: the watchdog 'Runtime Failure: <topic> stopped' (T0), the jetson_monitor log line showing GPU 99.7 %, and the camera-terminal errors. A spike within [T0-3 s, T0] is a cause candidate. A spike at about [T0+11 s, T0+60 s] is the relaunch itself (zed_watchdog_node.py:177-181, cooldown 10 s).

Add read-only logging on the Orin. Run `tegrastats --interval 100 --logfile` for clocks, GR3D % and temperatures. Set ZED `debug.sdk_verbose_log_file`. Run `ros2 topic echo /diagnostics` filtered on zed_front, and check `dmesg -T`. None of these change the Orin environment.

Replace the 3-topic, 3 s, kill-all watchdog with a staged per-camera supervisor. Pseudo-code:
```
PER_CAM = {front:{data:['.../point_cloud/cloud_registered','.../left/gray/rect/camera_info'], hb:'/zed_multi/zed_front/status/heartbeat'}, rear:{...}, right:{...}}
WARN_S=3.0; DATA_STALL_S=30.0 (>= SDK recovery; was 3); HB_DEAD_S=5.0; STABLE_RESET_S=600
loop @2 Hz (time.monotonic):
  for cam in cams:
    proc_alive = cam.proc.poll() is None
    hb_age = now-cam.hb_last; data_age = max(now-t for t in cam.data_last)
    if not proc_alive or hb_age>HB_DEAD_S: snapshot(cam,'DEAD'); restart(cam); continue   # immediate
    if data_age>WARN_S and not cam.warned: snapshot(cam,'SLOW') ; cam.warned=True        # log only
    if data_age>DATA_STALL_S: snapshot(cam,'STALLED'); restart(cam)                       # escalate
    if cam.state==RUNNING and now-cam.running_since>STABLE_RESET_S: cam.attempts=0
restart(cam): SIGINT process group -> wait 10 s -> SIGTERM -> wait 5 s -> SIGKILL; backoff = min(10*2**attempts, 120) s
snapshot(): last tegrastats line, per-topic ages, heartbeat age, last /diagnostics for that camera, tail of camera log, dmesg tail
```
Use callback groups with a MultiThreadedExecutor so reception never blocks on restarts. Subscribe to heartbeat (zed_msgs/Heartbeat, 1 Hz wall timer independent of grab, main.cpp:3424-3433) and to small topics instead of only full clouds. Use time.monotonic().

Make per-camera restart real by running each camera in its own process. Either pass a different container_name per camera, or leave it empty so zed_camera.launch.py creates its own container (zed_camera.launch.py:289-309), and launch 3 separate `ros2 launch` processes, one per camera, each in its own process group (subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True), no gnome-terminal). Drop respawn=True on the container (three_cams.launch.py:105). Measure GPU throughput versus a single process on the Orin first: separate CUDA contexts time-slice. If you keep the single container, use the composition services /zed_multi/zed_multi_container/_container/unload_node and load_node for a 'soft' per-camera restart, with process-kill as the fallback.

Kill gracefully. The current path SIGKILLs only `ros2 launch`, and the container is torn down indirectly by SIGHUP without sl::Camera::close() (zed_watchdog_node.py:226-261). Send SIGINT to the whole process group first, so the wrapper joins threads and closes the camera, and match component_container* explicitly.
Reset attempt_count after a stable period (e.g. 10 min in RUNNING), and on FATAL_ERROR keep retrying with a long backoff instead of idling forever (zed_watchdog_node.py:188-193).

Remove the TF false-trigger path. In publishPointCloud, look up with tf2::TimePointZero, or cache the static camera extrinsic once, instead of the exact image stamp with a 0.1 s timeout (video_depth.cpp:2518-2522). This is a wrapper patch, not an SDK change.

Reduce GPU pressure on the front pipeline if tegrastats confirms saturation before stalls. Options: front depth_mode NEURAL_LIGHT, or a lower grab resolution if the 2.95 m OD range allows; run jetson_clocks at boot (scripts/setup_hardware.sh exists but is not called from run_all_auto*.sh; confirm with the user that this does not count as changing the environment); keep FP32 DEIM-N, not S. Remember that the first launch after swapping the ONNX builds a TRT engine, which saturates the GPU and can exceed boot_timeout 60 s. Pre-warm once by hand before the watchdog runs.

Fix jetson_monitor so it can diagnose. Drop both timers to 1 Hz (they currently fork ping and chronyc every 100 ms; jetson_monitor_node.py:18-19, :77-117). Add GPU cur_freq, Tj temperature and throttle flags. Fix the UnboundLocalError for cpu_temp/fan_rpm when jtop is down (:144-150 vs :177/:191). Rename avg_60s, which is really about 6 s. Write the JSON to a rotating file so incidents can be correlated.

findings.topic: 1a. Grab loop error handling
findings.claim: There is one grab thread per camera (threadFunc_zedGrab). It calls mZed->grab() while holding mPtMutex. The error codes are handled as follows. CAMERA_REBOOTING logs 'Connection issue detected', sleeps 1 s and continues. CAMERA_NOT_INITIALIZED and FAILURE log 'Camera issue detected: ... Trying to recover the connection...', sleep 1 s and continue. CORRUPTED_FRAME logs 'Grab status degraded' and keeps processing the frame. Every other code logs 'Critical camera error: <code>. NODE KILLED.' and calls exit(EXIT_FAILURE). That includes CAMERA_NOT_DETECTED (the code grab() returns on a frame timeout), CUDA_ERROR and NOT_ENOUGH_GPU_MEMORY. A run of REBOOTING/FAILURE returns therefore produces a stall of ≥1 s per iteration with no crash. Three in a row is enough to trip the watchdog's 3.0 s msg_timeout.

findings.topic: 1b. exit() kills all three cameras
findings.claim: All three ZED components run in one process: component_container_isolated, /zed_multi/zed_multi_container. exit(EXIT_FAILURE), called from any camera's thread, terminates the whole process, so all three cameras die. The same goes for an SDK segfault. The container has respawn=True with respawn_delay=10 s, but the components are loaded by a separate LoadComposableNodes action. launch_ros does not reload components into a respawned container (open issue ros2/launch_ros#361), so the container comes back empty. That matches 'without the watchdog the zed node just died'.

findings.implication: One camera's fatal error or crash takes out all three. Without a reload mechanism, respawn alone does not recover them.

findings.topic: 1c. Other exit paths
findings.claim: Other exit(EXIT_FAILURE) paths. (1) The grab thread exits the process if startPosTracking fails 3 times. The counter is a function-local static, so all 3 camera objects in the process share it. (2) initNode exits if startCamera() returns false, which covers open timeout, DRIVER_FAILURE and calibration errors. (3) startCamera exits on any failed camera-setting call after open. (4) OD parameter-parsing exits. Paths (2)-(4) are startup-only. Path (1) runs in the grab loop and is startup-time in practice.

findings.topic: 1d. camera_timeout_sec / camera_max_reconnect are open-time only
findings.claim: general.camera_timeout_sec and camera_max_reconnect (front 35/7, rear/right 25/5) are used only in startCamera's open() retry loop. That loop sleeps camera_timeout_sec between attempts and gives up after max_reconnect*timeout. They play no part in runtime grab recovery. async_grab_camera_recovery is hard-coded to true. grab_compute_capping_fps is hard-coded to 0, and the yaml does not expose either one. One failed open of the front camera means a 35 s sleep before the retry, which pushes the 3 cameras close to the watchdog's 60 s boot_timeout.

findings.topic: 1e. async_grab_camera_recovery semantics (SDK 5.1.1)
findings.claim: With async_grab_camera_recovery=true, grab() returns CAMERA_REBOOTING after a short period on a communication issue, and recovery runs in the background. The wrapper turns each such return into a 1 s sleep. If the SDK keeps reporting REBOOTING, topics stay stalled with no crash, and only the watchdog restarts the cameras. SDK 5.2.1 release notes: 'Fixed an issue where GMSL2 cameras could stay in state sl::CAMERA_STATE::REBOOTING indefinitely.' 5.5.0: 'Fixed GMSL cameras (ZED X / ZED X One) occasionally freezing until reboot when the sensor emitted a spurious frame timestamp'. Both fixes are absent on 5.1.1.

findings.topic: 1f. enable_image_validity_check=1 and a known grab() lock
findings.claim: All three yamls set enable_image_validity_check: 1, which the wrapper passes to InitParameters. Per the SDK, this adds extra computation inside grab(). SDK 5.2.1 release notes: 'Fixed a rare lock that could appear using Camera::grab() when corrupted frame detector was enabled.' The 5.1.2 fix only covered the read()-only/close case. On 5.1.1 a grab() lock in the corrupted-frame detector is therefore a plausible silent per-camera stall: grab never returns, there is no error log, and the heartbeat timer keeps running.

findings.topic: 1g. Custom OD crash path on 5.1.1
findings.claim: Every frame that has a subscriber, the wrapper calls the deprecated retrieveCustomObjects(objects, CustomObjectDetectionRuntimeParameters, id), which re-sends the per-class runtime parameters each time. The zenoh allow-list bridges /zed_front/obj_det/objects, so that subscriber is effectively always present. (over hours). 5.1.2 also has 'Fixed a random crash when tracking objects whose estimators failed to initialize'. The robot runs 5.1.1. A segfault here would kill the whole container (see 1b). It is UNVERIFIED that passing unchanged params each frame triggers the bug.

findings.topic: 2a. Thread structure per camera
findings.claim: Each camera runs these threads. (1) The grab thread does grab() and then, in the same loop iteration and under mPtMutex, runs processVideoDepth (retrieveImage/retrieveMeasure to CPU), processPointCloud (retrieveMeasure XYZBGRA to CPU), processOdometry/Pose, processDetectedObjects (under mObjDetMutex) and processRtRoi. (2) The video/depth publish thread. (3) The point-cloud publish thread, which runs only when depth is enabled. (4) The sensors thread. (5) Timers on the node executor: heartbeat 1 Hz, temperature, diagnostics. Hand-off to the publisher threads uses try_lock: if the publisher thread still holds its mutex (it holds it while publishing and during its rate-control sleep), the grab thread skips that frame. It never blocks. So publishing cannot stall the grab loop. A watched topic only stops when the grab loop stops producing successful frames, or when a publisher thread is stuck.
findings.evidence: main.cpp:3389-3421 (initThreads), 4383-4775 (grab loop; 4513 lock_guard mPtMutex held to end of try; 4717 processVideoDepth, 4722 processPointCloud, 4750-4754 processDetectedObjects); video_depth.cpp:1424-1459 (vd try_lock), 2425-2464 (pc try_lock + retrieveMeasure CPU), 2968-2999 & 3297-3329 (publisher threads hold their mutex across the loop), 3100-3132 & 3270-3295 (rate sleep while holding the lock), main.cpp:3424-3434 (heartbeat timer 1000 ms).
findings.implication: A ≥3 s stall in a watched topic means grab() stopped returning SUCCESS for that camera (SDK/GPU/camera), or the cloud thread is dropping every frame (TF). It cannot come from simple publish backpressure.

findings.topic: 2b. OD is asynchronous to grab in the SDK
findings.claim: OD inference does not run synchronously inside the wrapper's grab loop. The SDK says retrieveObjects/retrieveCustomObjects 'immediately returns the last objects detected. If the current detection isn't done, the objects from the last detection will be returned, and Objects::is_new will be set to false', and runtime params are applied on the next inference 'since the processing is done in parallel'. 5.1.1 has no image_sync field in ObjectDetectionParameters. The heavier DEIM model (about 1.34x YOLO26n) therefore adds GPU contention, not direct blocking of grab. The exception is startup: startObjDetect(), which calls enableObjectDetection and so does TensorRT engine optimization or deserialization of the ONNX, is called from inside the front grab thread and blocks the front cloud until it finishes.
findings.evidence: Camera.hpp:12734-12737, 12764-12766, 12800-12806, 12712-12717; Camera.hpp:6752-6880 (no image_sync); main.cpp:4474-4483 (startObjDetect in grab thread); objdet.cpp:950-957 (custom_onnx_file -> enableObjectDetection); Camera.hpp ObjectDetectionParameters custom_onnx_file doc (engine optimized and cached; re-optimized if the ONNX weights change).
findings.implication: If the first run after the model swap has to optimize the DEIM engine on the Orin and that takes longer than the watchdog's boot_timeout (60 s), the watchdog kills it on every attempt and the cache never gets written. The build time on the Orin is UNVERIFIED.

findings.topic: 3a. GPU sharing between the 3 cameras
findings.claim: Each sl::Camera creates its own CUDA context unless sdk_cuda_ctx is supplied ('Leaving this parameter empty asks the SDK to create its own context'). The wrapper does not supply one (that code is commented out). The SDK docs do not say whether it is a separate context or the primary context: UNVERIFIED. If there are 3 contexts in one process, the GPU time-slices between them, so the front camera's heavy work (NEURAL depth + GEN_1 tracking + custom OD) delays rear (NEURAL_LIGHT) and right (depth NONE) GPU work. The right camera still does rectification and resize on retrieval. That work is very likely on the GPU but UNVERIFIED. The expected effect is lower frame rates and frame drops for all cameras, not a 3 s zero-output gap. A full 3 s gap on rear or right is much more consistent with an SDK/driver-level hang (1e/1f) than with plain contention.
findings.evidence: Camera.hpp:9838-9853 (sdk_cuda_ctx doc); main.cpp:2400-2404, 2425-2432 (custom context commented out), 2471 (sdk_gpu_id = -1 from yaml gpu_id: -1); common_stereo_zed_front.yaml:84,101,156-158; rear :84; right :84 (NONE); main.cpp:3414-3418 (no PC thread when depth disabled).
findings.implication: Which topic stalled first decides the question. If right/gray stalls, GPU load from front OD is unlikely to be the root cause.

findings.topic: 3b. InitParameters actually used

Per the SDK: grab_compute_capping_fps is an upper compute limit with no effect when the computation is already slower. async_image_retrieval decouples image retrieval rate from grab, meant for SVO/streaming. sdk_gpu_id is meaningless on a single-GPU Orin.

findings.topic: 4. Patched publishPointCloud TF drop
findings.claim: The patched publishPointCloud looks up base_link <- <cam>_left_camera_frame at the cloud's image timestamp, with a 0.1 s timeout. On any tf2::TransformException it logs 'Could not transform %s to base_link: %s', throttled to once per second and skipping the first occurrence, and returns without publishing. Clouds are absent for as long as the lookup keeps failing: indefinitely, with no retry limit and no fallback. Each failure blocks only that camera's cloud thread, for up to 0.1 s. If the transform comes from /tf_static (latched, never expires), a zenoh stall after the first reception has no effect. If any link in the chain comes over dynamic /tf, a zenoh delay or stall, or clock skew between the IPC and the Orin, makes lookups at the image stamp fail, and both front and rear clouds disappear while the right image keeps flowing. Each camera also creates a second TransformListener (tf_buffer_) besides mTfBuffer. The patched function has no try/catch around publish, unlike the image publishers.

Whether the IPC publishes these frames on /tf or /tf_static is UNVERIFIED (IPC side not in this repo).
findings.implication: A TF-caused stall looks like 'front and rear clouds stop, right image fine' plus 'Could not transform ...' warnings, and has nothing to do with GPU load.

findings.topic: 5a. Diagnostics and status topics
findings.claim: Topics that show which failure happened. (1) /diagnostics (diagnostic_updater, per camera). It shows 'Data Capture Mean Frequency', 'Tot. Processing Time', 'Frame Drop rate' (getFrameDroppedCount), 'Object detection Processing Time'. Summaries: 'System overloaded. Consider reducing ...' after ≥10 overloaded updates, 'Performance Degraded - Corrupted frame received', or the grab error string as ERROR. The 'Point Cloud Mean Frequency/Processing Time' fields are stale or garbage because the patched publishPointCloud no longer updates mPcPeriodMean_sec/mPcProcMean_sec. (2) /zed_multi/<cam>/status/heartbeat, a 1 Hz executor timer independent of the grab thread. If the heartbeat is alive while the camera's topics stop, the process is alive and the grab is stalled. If the heartbeat stops, the process died or hung. (3) /zed_multi/<cam>/status/health (low_image_quality etc.), published from the grab loop only when validity check >0 and there is a subscriber. All three need publish_status: true (set) and a subscriber.

In the launch output, 'process has died [pid ..., exit code N]' distinguishes the cases: N=1 is a wrapper exit(), -11 is an SDK segfault, -9 is the watchdog SIGKILL. Watchdog strings: 'Runtime Failure: <topic> stopped.', 'Unstable: <topic> stalled.', 'Boot Timeout'. check_topic_health returns the first stale topic in dict order (front cloud, rear cloud, right image), so if everything stalls at once it always reports front. SDK messages appear on stdout because sdk_verbose: 1, but sdk_verbose_log_file redirects all stdout of the process, so setting it affects all 3 cameras.

findings.topic: 5c. jetson_monitor reading
findings.claim: jetson_monitor publishes 'usage_percent' as int(gpu_cur) and 'avg_60s' as round(mean, 1) over a deque of 60 samples at a 0.1 s timer, which is about a 6 s window, not 60 s. A value like '99.7' with one decimal is therefore most likely avg_60s: about 6 s of saturated GPU, not 2-3 s. The jtop sample refresh rate is UNVERIFIED (likely slower than 10 Hz, so samples repeat). The monitor has no correlation with the watchdog timeline.
findings.evidence: jetson_monitor/jetson_monitor_node.py:17-18 (interval 0.1), 26-29 (deque maxlen 60), 140-141, 165-166, 180-182.
findings.implication: The order of events (GPU saturation before the stall, or GPU burst from the restart/startup itself after the watchdog fires) has to be established from timestamps. The 99.7 may be the effect, not the cause.

hypotheses.cause: The GPU spike is the restart, not its cause. After the watchdog fires (or after an SDK-internal camera recovery), 3 cameras reopen, the NEURAL/NEURAL_LIGHT depth models load, and the OD TensorRT engine is deserialized. That saturates the GPU for seconds.
hypotheses.mechanism: watchdog COOLDOWN -> relaunch -> startCamera/open + enableObjectDetection inside the grab thread (main.cpp:4474-4483). jetson_monitor's 6 s average then reads ~99.7.
hypotheses.how_to_confirm: Put timestamps side by side: watchdog 'Runtime Failure: X stopped' / 'Attempt N', jetson_monitor JSON 'timestamp', and `tegrastats --interval 100 --logfile` (read-only, on the Orin). If GPU 99% starts after the failure log, this hypothesis holds.
hypotheses.fix: No GPU fix needed. Find the real stall cause with the other hypotheses. Make sure the DEIM engine cache was built once before the watchdog runs, by launching without the watchdog and waiting for OD to start.

hypotheses.cause: SDK 5.1.1 grab() lock in the corrupted-frame detector (enable_image_validity_check: 1). Fixed in SDK 5.2.1.
hypotheses.mechanism: grab() never returns on one camera -> no images/clouds from it -> the 3 s watchdog timeout fires. No wrapper error is logged, the heartbeat keeps running, and the 1 Hz diagnostics keep the last status.
hypotheses.how_to_confirm: During a stall: heartbeat for that camera still at 1 Hz, no 'Connection issue'/'Critical' logs. If possible, `gdb -p <container pid> -batch -ex 'thread apply all bt'` or `eu-stack -p` (read-only) shows the grab thread blocked inside libsl_zed in the validity/corruption code. As a test, set enable_image_validity_check: 0 and see whether the restarts stop.
hypotheses.fix: Set general.enable_image_validity_check: 0 in all three common_stereo_zed_*.yaml (yaml only, no Orin stack change). This also removes some per-grab compute.

hypotheses.cause: GMSL camera stuck in REBOOTING, or a capture freeze, on SDK 5.1.1 / ZED X driver. Fixed in 5.2.1 and 5.5.0.
hypotheses.mechanism: async_grab_camera_recovery=true -> grab returns CAMERA_REBOOTING (or FAILURE) -> the wrapper sleeps 1 s per loop (main.cpp:4581-4596) -> topics stall indefinitely. Any GPU spike comes from the SDK's internal re-init.
hypotheses.how_to_confirm: grep the launch/terminal log and ~/.ros/log for 'Connection issue detected' or 'Camera issue detected'. /diagnostics summary shows ERROR with 'CAMERA REBOOTING'. Check `dmesg`/`journalctl -u zed_x_daemon` around the timestamp for GMSL/Argus errors.
hypotheses.fix: Treat as a camera-side fault. Keep the watchdog, but restart only the affected camera: run one container per camera (one process each) so the other two are unaffected. Optionally restart zed_x_daemon on repeated failure. An SDK upgrade is out of scope per the user.

hypotheses.cause: Crash in SDK custom OD (5.1.1) from re-sending CustomObjectDetectionRuntimeParameters every frame (fixed in 5.1.2), or the estimator-init crash (fixed in 5.1.2).
hypotheses.mechanism: retrieveCustomObjects(objects, params, id) is called each frame while /obj_det/objects has a subscriber (the zenoh bridge). A random segfault after hours kills the whole container, so all 3 cameras go. respawn brings back an empty container (launch_ros#361). This is the 'node just died' case.
hypotheses.how_to_confirm: Launch log shows 'process has died ... exit code -11' (or -6) with no 'Critical camera error' line before it. Check for core dumps / `coredumpctl list` and dmesg segfault lines in libsl_zed or the TensorRT libs.
hypotheses.fix: Wrapper patch: call setCustomObjectDetectionRuntimeParameters(mCustomOdProperties, mObjDetInstID) once after enableObjectDetection and on dynamic-param change, then use retrieveObjects(objects, mObjDetInstID) per frame (Camera.hpp:12731, 12760, deprecation note 12816-12817). Optionally split cameras into separate processes.

hypotheses.cause: Wrapper exit() on a 'critical' grab code (CAMERA_NOT_DETECTED, CUDA_ERROR, NOT_ENOUGH_GPU_MEMORY, ...) under load.
hypotheses.mechanism: main.cpp:4604-4611 calls exit(EXIT_FAILURE) from the grab thread, which kills all 3 cameras. respawn does not reload the components.
hypotheses.how_to_confirm: Log line 'Critical camera error: <CODE>. NODE KILLED.' followed by 'process has died ... exit code 1'.
hypotheses.fix: Patch the handler to treat CAMERA_NOT_DETECTED/CUDA_ERROR like the recoverable codes (log, back off, and after N consecutive failures close/reopen only that camera), instead of exit(). Use separate containers per camera.

hypotheses.cause: Plain GPU over-subscription after the DEIM swap (front NEURAL + GEN_1 tracking + FP32 custom OD + rear NEURAL_LIGHT + validity checks).
hypotheses.mechanism: Time-sliced GPU between camera contexts (separate contexts UNVERIFIED) -> longer grab/retrieve for all cameras -> lower rates and frame drops. A full 3 s gap from this alone is unlikely but possible under bursts.
hypotheses.how_to_confirm: Before incidents, /diagnostics 'Data Capture Mean Frequency' < 15 Hz, 'Tot. Processing Time' > 0.067 s, 'System overloaded', rising 'Frame Drop rate'. `ros2 topic hz` on the 3 watched topics shows a degraded rate rather than a clean stop. tegrastats GR3D near 99% continuously, not only at restarts.
hypotheses.fix: Reduce GPU load with yaml changes only: front depth_mode NEURAL -> NEURAL_LIGHT, disable the validity check, lower point_cloud_res or the publish resolution. Re-evaluate whether front positional tracking and OD tracking are needed. jetson_clocks would pin clocks but changes the Orin's runtime config, so it needs the user's explicit consent. FP16 is not an option for DEIM on TRT 10.3.

hypotheses.cause: TF from the IPC (zenoh) missing or late, so the patched publishPointCloud drops every cloud.
hypotheses.mechanism: lookupTransform(base_link, <cam>_left_camera_frame, image stamp, 0.1 s) throws -> return (video_depth.cpp:2516-2530). Front and rear clouds stop and the right image continues. This is unrelated to GPU.
hypotheses.how_to_confirm: Log has 'Could not transform zed_front_left_camera_frame to base_link' / rear. Check whether these frames are on /tf_static or /tf (`ros2 topic echo /tf_static --once`, `ros2 run tf2_ros tf2_echo base_link zed_front_left_camera_frame`), and check the IPC/Orin clock offset.
hypotheses.fix: Publish the camera mounts on /tf_static from the IPC, or have the wrapper cache the last good static transform and use lookupTransform at tf2::TimePointZero (latest) for a fixed mount, instead of dropping the cloud.

recommendations: Step 1, discriminate before changing anything (all read-only on the Orin). On the next incident, collect: (a) the watchdog line 'Runtime Failure: <topic> stopped'. It is biased toward front when all stall (zed_watchdog_node.py:219-224), so also log the age of all 3 topics. (b) The launch-output 'process has died ... exit code' (1 = wrapper exit, -11 = SDK segfault, -9 = watchdog). (c) A grep for 'Connection issue detected|Camera issue detected|Grab status degraded|Critical camera error|Object Detection error|Could not transform'. (d) A rosbag of /diagnostics, /zed_multi/*/status/heartbeat and the 3 watched topics. (e) `tegrastats --interval 100 --logfile` with timestamps to order GPU saturation against the failure.

Step 2, yaml-only: set general.enable_image_validity_check: 0 on all three cameras. It removes the SDK 5.1.1 grab() corrupted-frame-detector lock path (fixed only in 5.2.1) and some per-grab compute. Cost: the status/health topic and CORRUPTED_FRAME warnings go away.

Step 3, small wrapper patch (objdet.cpp:1079-1088): stop sending CustomObjectDetectionRuntimeParameters every frame. Call setCustomObjectDetectionRuntimeParameters once after enableObjectDetection and in handleCustomOdDynamicParams, then call retrieveObjects(objects, mObjDetInstID). This avoids the 5.1.1 custom-OD random crash fixed in 5.1.2.

Step 4, structural: run each camera in its own container process (three ComposableNodeContainers, or standalone zed_wrapper nodes). Then an exit() or segfault in front OD cannot take down the rear and right cameras, and the watchdog can restart only the failed camera. Also replace exit(EXIT_FAILURE) at main.cpp:4604-4611 with log + back-off + close/reopen of that camera.

Step 5, GPU headroom if diagnostics show overload: front depth_mode NEURAL -> NEURAL_LIGHT (rear already uses it), keep OD FP32, and consider whether front positional tracking or OD tracking can be dropped. Then re-measure DEIM latency on the Orin with trtexec (TRT 10.3) against YOLO26n under the same 3-camera load.

Step 6, watchdog hardening: use the per-camera status/heartbeat topics to tell 'process alive but grab stalled' from 'process dead'. Log the stalled-topic ages for all 3. Reset attempt_count after a period in RUNNING. Consider msg_timeout of about 5 s, because the wrapper's own REBOOTING/FAILURE recovery sleeps 1 s per attempt. Make sure the DEIM engine cache is built before the watchdog's 60 s boot_timeout applies (first launch manually).

Step 7, TF: confirm the base_link -> zed_*_left_camera_frame chain arrives on /tf_static. If it arrives on /tf, change the IPC to /tf_static, or patch publishPointCloud to use a cached static transform (TimePointZero) instead of dropping clouds.

Do not upgrade the SDK/JetPack (user constraint). Several relevant fixes exist only in 5.1.2/5.2.1/5.5.0 (custom-OD crash, grab lock with the corrupted-frame detector, GMSL stuck REBOOTING/freeze). This is the main argument the user can weigh later if the yaml and wrapper mitigations do not suffice. jetson_clocks also changes the Orin runtime config and needs the user's explicit OK.

findings.topic: Normal GPU load is far below 100%: 99.7% is a burst, an event, or low-clock behavior
findings.claim: Stereolabs' published per-mode numbers put the steady depth load for this setup well below saturation. On AGX Orin with ZED X at 30 FPS, NEURAL with 4 cameras is 53% GPU and NEURAL_LIGHT with 4 cameras is 46%. This robot runs 1x NEURAL (front, 15 fps), 1x NEURAL_LIGHT (rear, 15 fps) and 1x depth NONE (right). That is roughly a quarter to a third of the documented 4-camera, 30 fps load. DEIM-N adds an estimated 5.6-7.6 ms every 66.7 ms (about 8-11% duty at full clock). At full GPU clock the steady total should therefore sit well below 100%. A 2-3 s plateau at 99.7% needs either a burst of extra GPU work, a different consumer, or a GPU running at a reduced clock or throttled.
findings.evidence: https://docs.stereolabs.com/docs/depth-sensing/depth-modes (NEURAL_LIGHT on Orin AGX: 1 cam 11% GPU, 4 cams 46%; NEURAL on Orin AGX: 4 cams at 30 FPS, 53% GPU; NEURAL_PLUS: 4 cams 97%). Configs: common_stereo_zed_front.yaml:84 depth_mode 'NEURAL'; common_stereo_zed_rear.yaml:84 'NEURAL_LIGHT'; common_stereo_zed_right.yaml:84 'NONE'; zedx_zed_*.yaml:10 grab_frame_rate 15. The documentation numbers are probably for the current SDK (5.5) and their clock settings are not stated, so they are UNVERIFIED for 5.1.1.
findings.implication: Don't assume the DEIM model 'fills' the GPU. Before changing models, record GPU frequency, throttling state and the exact event timeline (see the recommendations).

findings.topic: jtop GPU% is busy-time, not normalized to clock frequency
findings.claim: jetson_monitor publishes jtop stats['GPU'], which is GR3D busy-time as a percentage. It is not normalized to frequency, so at a low DVFS clock (Orin minimum ≈306 MHz against a MAXN max of 1301 MHz) the same work reads as a much higher %. jtop refreshes every 1.0 s by default while jetson_monitor polls every 0.1 s, so '2-3 s at 99.7' means 2-3 consecutive 1-s jtop samples. The Orin GPU devfreq governor scales freely under MAXN unless jetson_clocks is set. One user with 4x ZED X on an AGX Orin 64GB saw the governor stay at the 306 MHz minimum under full SDK load; that is a user observation, not confirmed by Stereolabs.
findings.evidence: jetson_monitor/jetson_monitor/jetson_monitor_node.py:18 (interval 0.1), :36-37 (jtop() with default interval), :140 (stats['GPU']). jtop docs: 'class jtop.jtop(interval=1.0)', https://rnext.it/jetson_stats/reference/jtop.html. NVIDIA tegrastats doc: GR3D_FREQ = 'Proportion of GPU activation time in a period', format 'GR3D_FREQ X%@[Y1,Y2]' (per-GPC MHz), https://docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r36.4/DeveloperGuide/AT/JetsonLinuxDevelopmentTools/TegrastatsUtility.html. AGX Orin 64GB MAXN GPU max 1301 MHz; cur_freq at /sys/devices/platform/17000000.gpu/devfreq/17000000.gpu/cur_freq; load in /sys/devices/platform/17000000.gpu/load (value/10 = %), https://docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r36.4/DeveloperGuide/SD/PlatformPowerAndPerformance/JetsonOrinNanoSeriesJetsonOrinNxSeriesAndJetsonAgxOrinSeries.html. The 306 MHz observation is from https://community.stereolabs.com/t/62-frame-drops-with-auto-exposure-enabled-on-4x-zed-x-gmsl2-data-attached/10853. Whether this robot's GPU sits at a low clock is UNVERIFIED.
findings.implication: Have jetson_monitor also log jetson.gpu['gpu']['freq']['cur'/'min'/'max'/'governor'] (or run tegrastats --interval 100) so a '99.7%' spike can be classified as either 'saturated at 1301 MHz' or 'busy at a low or throttled clock'. Thermal throttling is unlikely below 99 °C (SW throttle threshold). Over-current throttling (OC3 halves CPU+GPU when the 65 W instantaneous limit is exceeded) can be checked read-only via /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*/oc*_event_cnt.

findings.topic: Watchdog design: one 3-s gap on any of 3 topics kills all 3 cameras
findings.claim: zed_watchdog marks a failure as soon as any one of the 3 watched topics has had no message for more than msg_timeout = 3.0 s. It then SIGKILLs the whole multi-camera launch (all three cameras share one component_container_isolated process) and relaunches after a 10 s cooldown. The relaunch itself causes a large GPU burst: 3x CUDA/SDK init, NEURAL and NEURAL_LIGHT engine load, custom ONNX engine load, and positional tracking init. It also takes at least 10 s plus boot time. The wrapper sets async_grab_camera_recovery = true, so on a GMSL/Argus hiccup the SDK recovers in the background and grab() returns CAMERA_REBOOTING. The wrapper then sleeps 1 s and retries, so topics stop during recovery. Stereolabs staff say this recovery normally takes 20-30 s, so the 3 s watchdog always pre-empts the SDK's own recovery.
findings.evidence: zed_watchdog/config/zed_watchdog_default.yaml:13-22 (3 topics, msg_timeout 3.0, cooldown 10, boot_timeout 60, max_attempts 50); zed_watchdog/zed_watchdog/zed_watchdog_node.py:164-171 (RUNNING → COOLDOWN on any stalled topic), :211-217 and :263-275 (cleanup kills everything), :226-261 (kills by process name / launch cmdline); zed_multi_camera_delay_separate_three_cams.launch.py:93 (component_container_isolated), :98-107 (single container, respawn=True, respawn_delay 10). zed_camera_component_main.cpp:2484-2486 (async_grab_camera_recovery = true), :4581-4587 (CAMERA_REBOOTING → log, sleep 1 s, continue). Staff quote 'Normally, you must wait for it to recover. 20-30 sec is the expected period' and 'you are overloading the Jetson, and this could cause the ZED X Driver to timeout and issue a camera reboot to recover': https://community.stereolabs.com/t/error-code-camera-rebooting-when-streaming-multiple-cameras-over-jetson/9445
findings.implication: Part of the problem is self-inflicted. A transient 2-3 s stall turns into a full restart of all 3 cameras plus a startup GPU burst. Even with no other changes, raising msg_timeout (e.g. 6-10 s), letting CAMERA_REBOOTING recovery finish, and restarting only on real process death or a long stall would remove most restarts. This is a mitigation; it does not fix the cause.

findings.topic: Why 'without the watchdog the ZED node just died'
findings.claim: In the grab loop, any grab() error other than END_OF_SVOFILE_REACHED, CAMERA_REBOOTING, CAMERA_NOT_INITIALIZED, FAILURE or CORRUPTED_FRAME logs 'Critical camera error ... NODE KILLED.' and calls exit(EXIT_FAILURE). Examples are CUDA_ERROR, NOT_ENOUGH_GPU_MEMORY and CAMERA_NOT_DETECTED. Because all three cameras are components in one container process, exit() kills all three. A same-stack forum report (AGX Orin 64GB, L4T 36.4.7, SDK 5.1.1, 3x ZED X via Quad card) shows container death with exit code -6 (abort). Staff blamed GEN_3 positional tracking on 5.1.1; this robot uses GEN_1, so that specific cause does not apply. SDK 5.1.2, which is not installed, fixed 'a random crash occurring when using Custom Object Detection and repeatedly setting custom parameters' and 'a random crash when tracking objects whose estimators failed to initialize'. The wrapper passes CustomObjectDetectionRuntimeParameters (mCustomOdProperties) on every retrieveCustomObjects() call, every frame, and front OD tracking is on.
findings.evidence: zed_camera_component_main.cpp:4597-4611 (else-branch: 'Critical camera error ... NODE KILLED.' then exit(EXIT_FAILURE)); zed_camera_component_objdet.cpp:1080-1088 (runtime custom params set every call); common_stereo_zed_front.yaml:157 enable_tracking true; SDK 5.1.2 notes, https://www.stereolabs.com/en-gr/developers/release/5.1; same-stack thread https://community.stereolabs.com/t/ros2-humble-zed-multi-container-dies-frequently-jetson-agx-orin-64gb-l4t-36-4-7-zed-sdk-5-1-1-3-zedx-mini-via-quad-capture-card/10374. Whether the 5.1.1 crash bugs are triggered by the wrapper's per-frame parameter passing is UNVERIFIED.
findings.implication: Container deaths and GPU spikes may have different causes. Check the container exit code and the last log line ('NODE KILLED' with the error code, or a signal -6/-11) to separate 'grab error → exit' from 'SDK 5.1.1 crash'. Turning off OD tracking removes one of the two 5.1.1 crash paths fixed in 5.1.2.

findings.topic: Auto-exposure I2C frame drops on ZED X driver < 1.4.0 (robot has 1.3.2)
findings.claim: Stereolabs confirmed that on ZED X drivers older than 1.4.0, I2C traffic from auto-exposure and IMU reads causes grab() frame drops in multi-camera GMSL setups. One case measured 62% drops and gaps up to 700 ms with AE on, and 0% drops with exposure locked. The fix is driver 1.4.0, which is forbidden here. The config-level workaround is locked exposure. All three cameras here run auto_exposure_gain and auto_whitebalance as true, and the installed ZED Link Quad package is 1.3.2.
findings.evidence: Staff (mattrouss): 'This issue has indeed been identified in driver versions <1.4.0', 'the source of these drops was related to the I2C communications made for both the auto-exposure' (and IMU); data: AE on 62-63% drop / 700 ms max gap, AE locked 0%. https://community.stereolabs.com/t/62-frame-drops-with-auto-exposure-enabled-on-4x-zed-x-gmsl2-data-attached/10853. Config: common_stereo_zed_{front,rear,right}.yaml:43 auto_exposure_gain true, :46 auto_whitebalance true; manual values already present in zedx_zed_*.yaml:13 exposure_time 2000, :17 analog_gain 2000. Driver 1.3.2 is from the CLAUDE.md bring-up files (stereolabs-zedlink-quad_1.3.2...deb).
findings.implication: This is a non-GPU source of grab stalls that fits the robot's driver version. The setup in that thread (4 cameras, 1080p30, cameras moving) is heavier than this one, so the effect size here is UNVERIFIED. Indoor fab lighting is steady, so locked exposure/gain/WB on all 3 cameras is a cheap config-only test.

findings.topic: Per-feature GPU cost and burstiness (current values → cheaper alternatives)
findings.claim:
Current settings, cost and burstiness per feature:
- NEURAL depth (front) and NEURAL_LIGHT (rear) are fixed-cost networks every frame: steady, not bursty. NEURAL_LIGHT is the documented 'fastest, best for multi-camera' mode, with accuracy under 1% error at 0.3-3 m. That covers front's max_depth of 3.0 m, so moving front to NEURAL_LIGHT is the biggest documented depth saving (46% vs 53% for 4 cams at 30 fps on AGX, about 13% relative). NEURAL_PLUS should be avoided.
- depth_stabilization is already 0 (the SDK default is 30). This means no temporal filter and no forced positional tracking.
- Positional tracking (front only): GEN_1, area_memory false, imu_fusion false. With no area memory there is no loop-closure or relocalization burst. GEN_1 'computes depth and therefore uses the GPU'. Front positional tracking is likely only needed because OD enable_tracking requires it (the Stereolabs API docs say to enable positional tracking before object tracking). Do not switch to GEN_3 on 5.1.1 (staff-identified crash).
- OD: custom FP32 DEIM-N on 640x640 at every grab, plus SDK tracking, NMS3D filtering and max_range 2.95. Inference runs every frame (steady). Neither the SDK 5.x ObjectDetectionParameters nor the wrapper has a detection-rate or 'every N frames' parameter, and image_sync is not in the 5.x field list.
- Point cloud: COMPACT = 448x256 (NEURAL_W/2 x NEURAL_H/2), retrieved to CPU in the grab thread every frame, then a CPU transform/voxel step. Mostly CPU. REDUCED (224x128) quarters it, and right already uses REDUCED.
- Image validity check = 1 on all cameras ('requires some computations', runs in grab).
- grab_compute_capping_fps is hard-coded to 0 in the wrapper, so it cannot be changed from YAML.
- Front grabs HD1200 (1920x1200) but publishes 960x600. The wrapper already sets maximum_working_resolution to max(pub, pc) = 960x600, so internal processing is likely limited. Grabbing SVGA natively (960x600 binned, pub_downscale_factor 1.0) would cut capture/ISP/rectify bandwidth by 4x, at the cost of a different calibration mode and image quality (UNVERIFIED effect on DEIM AP).
- Event-type (bursty) GPU loads: camera open, self-calibration (already off), NEURAL/ONNX engine deserialization at every (re)launch, TensorRT engine build for a new or changed custom ONNX on first load (minutes, see the next finding), and camera recovery after CAMERA_REBOOTING (re-init). Auto exposure is I2C/CPU-side, not GPU.

Wrapper: zed_camera_component_main.cpp:2454 grab_compute_capping_fps = 0.0f (hard-coded), :2489-2494 maximum_working_resolution, :4722 processPointCloud and :4752 processDetectedObjects in the grab thread; zed_camera_component_video_depth.cpp:2433-2435 CPU retrieve; sl_types.hpp:196-197 NEURAL_W/H 896x512. SDK docs: PositionalTrackingParameters 'GEN_1 computes depth and therefore uses the GPU', https://www.stereolabs.com/docs/api/structsl_1_1PositionalTrackingParameters.html; InitParameters image validity and capping, https://www.stereolabs.com/docs/api/structsl_1_1InitParameters.html; OD tracking needs positional tracking, https://docs.stereolabs.com/docs/development/zed-sdk/modules/object-detection/using-the-api; ObjectDetectionParameters field list (no rate field), https://www.stereolabs.com/docs/api/structsl_1_1ObjectDetectionParameters.html; staff: 'you can reduce their usage by capping the FPS' via grab_compute_capping_fps, https://community.stereolabs.com/t/performance-on-agx-orin/4406. Per-feature ms costs on Orin for 5.1.1 are not published (UNVERIFIED).
findings.implication: In steady state the ZED pipeline's GPU work per frame is roughly constant. The only config levers that clearly cut it are front NEURAL → NEURAL_LIGHT, OD tracking and positional tracking off on front, point cloud REDUCED, validity check off, and front grab SVGA. A 2-3 s spike from these steady features alone is unlikely, so look for an event (recovery/relaunch/engine build), another GPU client, or a clock drop.

findings.topic: Custom ONNX TensorRT engine build on first load (DEIM swap)
findings.claim: On first use of a custom ONNX, the SDK builds a TensorRT engine for the GPU. Stereolabs states the optimized model is saved and reused, and that changing the weights at the same path triggers re-optimization. The docs say optimized models are stored in /usr/local/zed/resources as dot-prefixed files, plus a '.*_timing_cache'. Optimization 'may take a long time' and staff advise avoiding other GPU tasks while it runs. If the build for DEIM-N FP32 on TRT 10.3 takes longer than the watchdog boot_timeout (60 s), the watchdog kills the launch mid-build. That can repeat the build (100% GPU for minutes) on every attempt. The same happens if the engine file cannot be written. Build duration on Orin for this DETR, and whether 5.1.1 caches custom engines in the same folder, are UNVERIFIED.
findings.evidence: ObjectDetectionParameters.custom_onnx_file: 'The resulting optimized model will be saved for re-use in the future' and re-optimization on changed weights, https://www.stereolabs.com/docs/api/structsl_1_1ObjectDetectionParameters.html; 'The optimized model will be saved in the /usr/local/zed/resources folder and reused in subsequent runs', https://docs.stereolabs.com/docs/integrations/ros-2/object-detection-and-tracking; dot-prefixed files and timing cache (staff adujardin), https://community.stereolabs.com/t/copying-optimized-models-from-one-machine-to-another/10126; 'avoid using GPU-related tasks when optimizing the models', https://community.stereolabs.com/t/whats-the-meaning-of-optimization-in-the-context-of-the-zed-ai-modules/6120; watchdog boot_timeout 60 s at zed_watchdog_default.yaml:19 and zed_watchdog_node.py:141-144. SDK 5.5 adds sl::optimizeCustomAIModel() for ahead-of-time optimization, which is not available on 5.1.1 (https://www.stereolabs.com/developers/release).
findings.implication: After every ONNX change, check that a new dot-file appeared in /usr/local/zed/resources (ls -la, read-only) and that the first launch was allowed to finish optimizing with the watchdog stopped. If restarts cluster right after the model swap or after reboots, this is the cause. It does not explain sporadic 2-3 s spikes during steady running.

findings.topic: Lowering DEIM cost without FP16
findings.claim:
Config-only options for DEIM:
- Raise only the effective rate. grab_frame_rate is already at the HD1200/SVGA minimum of 15, and grab_compute_capping_fps is hard-coded to 0, so a lower OD rate needs a wrapper code change (set grab_compute_capping_fps, e.g. 10). Whether skipping retrieveCustomObjects() skips inference is UNVERIFIED, because detection may be triggered inside grab().
- Disable OD tracking, which also lets front positional tracking (GEN_1) be turned off.
- Use a smaller input. Detections are capped at max_range 2.95 m, so people appear large. A 512 (or 480) export costs about (512/640)^2 ≈ 0.64x the FLOPs. This needs a re-export with eval_spatial_size baked in, and ideally a fine-tune at that size; the AP impact is UNVERIFIED.
- Move the depth budget, i.e. front NEURAL → NEURAL_LIGHT, to free GPU for OD.
- DEIM-S would be about 2.2x N's latency and the wrong direction here.
findings.evidence: custom_object_detection.yaml:15-17 (onnx, input 640), :31 conf 80, :34 tracking_timeout 0.5; common_stereo_zed_front.yaml:157 enable_tracking true, :159 max_range 2.95; zed_camera_component_main.cpp:2454 (capping fps hard-coded 0); wrapper passes custom_onnx_dynamic_input_shape = custom_onnx_input_size at zed_camera_component_objdet.cpp:951-953. The 1.34x YOLO26n ratio for DEIM-N and the S-model ratio come from the CLAUDE.md measurements.
findings.implication: At 5.6-7.6 ms per 66.7 ms frame, DEIM alone is not enough to reach 100% at full clock. Shrinking the model is a secondary lever. Do the measurements (clock, timeline) first.

findings.topic: Non-GPU stall path: point cloud dropped when TF lookup fails
findings.claim: The patched publishPointCloud() looks up base_link → camera frame at the camera image timestamp with a 0.1 s wait. On any tf2 exception it silently drops the cloud (a throttled WARN 'Could not transform ... to base_link'). Two of the three watched topics are these clouds. TF comes from the IPC over zenoh, and Orin/IPC clocks are synced with chrony (jetson_monitor reads chronyc tracking). If the transform is on /tf rather than /tf_static, or zenoh/TF delivery hiccups or the clocks skew, front and rear clouds both stop. That trips the 3 s watchdog with no GPU cause.
findings.evidence: zed_camera_component_video_depth.cpp:2514-2529 (lookupTransform(..., current_timestamp, 0.1 s); return on exception); zed_watchdog_default.yaml:14-15 (watched cloud topics); jetson_monitor_node.py:98 (chronyc tracking), :192 time_offset_ms. Whether base_link→zed_*_left_camera_frame is static on the IPC is UNVERIFIED.
findings.implication: When a restart happens, check the zed log for 'Could not transform' warnings and which topic the watchdog named ('Runtime Failure: <topic> stopped'). If both clouds stop while the right gray image keeps flowing, it is TF or depth, not GMSL/Argus.

findings.topic: Known Stereolabs guidance for multiple ZED X on one Orin
findings.claim:
Stereolabs guidance for several ZED X on one Orin:
- Use NEURAL_LIGHT for multi-camera.
- Cap FPS with grab_compute_capping_fps to reduce CPU/GPU usage.
- Overload can make the ZED X driver time out and reboot the camera (CAMERA_REBOOTING, 20-30 s recovery).
- Use MAXN with jetson_clocks.
- SDK 5.1.0 'Enhanced GMSL camera acquisition ... fewer frame drops'; 5.1.1 only fixed GEN_3 and NEURAL min-depth issues.
- Later SDKs (5.2: 51-85% lower CPU, 5-45% lower grab latency on Jetson AGX; 5.5: improved GMSL capture latency, a fix for GMSL cameras 'occasionally freezing until reboot', INT8 NEURAL depth) are out of scope because no upgrades are allowed.
- Long-run nvargus/FUSA crashes with 3-4 ZED X on AGX Orin L4T 36.4.x are reported with no Stereolabs fix.
findings.evidence: https://docs.stereolabs.com/docs/depth-sensing/depth-modes; https://community.stereolabs.com/t/performance-on-agx-orin/4406 (alassagne: 'you can reduce their usage by capping the FPS', '15FPS with 4 cameras'); https://community.stereolabs.com/t/error-code-camera-rebooting-when-streaming-multiple-cameras-over-jetson/9445; https://www.stereolabs.com/en-gr/developers/release/5.1; https://community.stereolabs.com/t/release-5-2-is-out/10775 (via search summary); https://www.stereolabs.com/developers/release (5.5.0); https://community.stereolabs.com/t/nvargus-daemon-crash-after-20-45-min-with-4x-zed-x-8-gmsl2-streams-on-agx-orin-l4t-36-4-4/10839; MAXN + jetson_clocks tip summarized from https://community.stereolabs.com/t/improving-fps-on-jetson-orin-hw-with-zed-ros2-wrapper/2545 search results (exact staff wording UNVERIFIED).
findings.implication: Under the no-upgrade constraint, the levers are lower load (NEURAL_LIGHT, fewer modules, capped fps), steady clocks (jetson_clocks, with approval), locked exposure, and a watchdog that tolerates the SDK's own recovery.

hypotheses.cause: The 99.7% spike follows the stall instead of causing it. A GMSL/Argus capture hiccup (e.g. AE I2C traffic on driver 1.3.2, or an overload-induced driver timeout) makes the SDK recover in the background (CAMERA_REBOOTING). Topics stop for more than 3 s, the watchdog kills and relaunches all 3 cameras, and the relaunch (3x SDK init, NEURAL/NEURAL_LIGHT/ONNX engine deserialization, positional tracking init) produces the multi-second GPU plateau seen in jetson_monitor.
hypotheses.mechanism: zed_camera_component_main.cpp:4581-4587 returns CAMERA_REBOOTING with a 1 s sleep loop and no publishing, then zed_watchdog_node.py:164-171 triggers on a 3 s gap → kill all → relaunch after 10 s cooldown. Engine loading at startup is GPU-heavy. The AE/I2C drop mechanism is confirmed by Stereolabs for drivers below 1.4.0.
hypotheses.how_to_confirm: Align timestamps: watchdog log ('Runtime Failure: <topic> stopped', 'Launching'), zed container log ('Connection issue detected: CAMERA_REBOOTING', 'Grab status degraded', Argus timeout lines; set debug.sdk_verbose_log_file to a file), journalctl for nvargus-daemon/zed_x_daemon, and jetson_monitor GPU samples. If the GPU spike starts at or after 'Launching' or the CAMERA_REBOOTING lines, it is an effect.
hypotheses.fix: Raise msg_timeout (e.g. 8-10 s) and/or skip restart while the container is alive and logging CAMERA_REBOOTING (let the SDK's 20-30 s recovery finish). Restart only on process death or a long stall. Restart only the affected camera if possible: a per-camera container or load/unload of one component (code/launch change). Lock exposure/gain/WB on all cameras (auto_exposure_gain false, auto_whitebalance false, using zedx_zed_*.yaml exposure_time/analog_gain).

hypotheses.cause: The GPU runs at a low or throttled DVFS clock (MAXN without jetson_clocks, or OC/thermal throttling). Normal per-frame work then reads as 99% busy and grab latency stretches, which can tip the GMSL driver into timeout/recovery.
hypotheses.mechanism: GR3D% is busy time, not normalized to frequency. nvhost_podgov may sit near 306 MHz or ramp late (one user saw the minimum under full SDK load). OC3 halves CPU+GPU clocks above 65 W. At low clock, NEURAL + DEIM FP32 + 3 camera pipelines can exceed 66.7 ms per frame.
hypotheses.how_to_confirm: All read-only: `cat /sys/devices/platform/17000000.gpu/devfreq/17000000.gpu/{governor,cur_freq,min_freq,max_freq,available_frequencies}` (the path can differ on JP6; locate it with `ls /sys/class/devfreq/`). Run `tegrastats --interval 100` during operation and look at GR3D_FREQ X%@[MHz,MHz] and EMC_FREQ. Also check `nvpmodel -q`, `/sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*/oc*_event_cnt` before and after an event, and `/sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*/{type,temp}`. Optionally log jtop gpu freq cur/min/max in jetson_monitor.
hypotheses.fix: With the user's explicit approval, since it changes runtime state: run jetson_clocks, or raise only the GPU min_freq through devfreq sysfs. Otherwise reduce load (front NEURAL_LIGHT, OD tracking and positional tracking off, point cloud REDUCED) so that even a lower clock stays within the 66.7 ms budget.

hypotheses.cause: First-load TensorRT optimization of the new DEIM ONNX is interrupted or repeated. The build takes longer than boot_timeout 60 s, or the engine cache cannot be written, so every launch rebuilds at 100% GPU and the watchdog kills it.
hypotheses.mechanism: The SDK builds a TRT engine for a new or changed custom ONNX and stores it in /usr/local/zed/resources. zed_watchdog_node.py:141-144 kills the launch 60 s after start if not all topics are flowing.
hypotheses.how_to_confirm: Check whether restarts cluster right after the model swap or after reboots. Look in the zed log for optimization progress messages, and check that a new dot-file appeared in /usr/local/zed/resources with `ls -la --time-style=full-iso`, with a timestamp matching the first DEIM launch (read-only).

hypotheses.cause: Random crashes in SDK 5.1.1 custom OD and OD tracking (fixed only in 5.1.2), triggered by the wrapper passing custom runtime params on every frame and by OD tracking. These cause 'node simply died' events independently of GPU load.
